title: setNudgeSplit(>0) does not require nudge != address(0) — enabling the split before wiring the recipient bricks every yielding claim (NudgeNotConfigured)
description: setNudgeSplit (L396-402) validates only `_split > 100` (InvalidNudgeSplit) and never checks nudge != address(0). The coupling invariant (split>0 requires a nudge address) is enforced only on the READ side — claim() L506 `if (nudgeSplit > 0 && nudge == address(0)) revert NudgeNotConfigured()` — so the contract permits entering the inconsistent state on the write side. The L506 revert itself is INTENDED and documented (IStableYieldAccumulator L276-279; story-023 FAITHFUL); the gap is purely that the setter does not enforce it, leaving a non-obvious brick window. setNudgeAddress (L385-389) symmetrically allows clearing nudge to address(0) while a split is active.
impact: No value loss. Availability only: while the inconsistent (nudgeSplit>0, nudge==address(0)) state holds, every yielding claim runs the skim loop and NFT-balance check then reverts NudgeNotConfigured at L506 — atomically, so no NFT is consumed and no funds move. The permissionless claim path (the contract's sole purpose) is fully bricked for yielding claims until the owner sets a valid nudge address or returns the split to 0. Owner-self-inflicted, immediately owner-recoverable by a single setter.
attackPath: 1. Owner calls setNudgeSplit(20) to route 20% to a nudge recipient, before wiring the recipient (L396 only checks _split > 100, no nudge!=0 guard).
3. Any claim with yield runs the skim loop + NFT-balance check, then reverts NudgeNotConfigured at L506 (atomic rollback; NFT preserved).
4. All yielding claims revert until the owner sets a valid nudge address or sets nudgeSplit(0). The same brick arises if the owner later calls setNudgeAddress(0) without first zeroing the split.
recommendation: Enforce the invariant on the write side so the inconsistent state is unreachable: in setNudgeSplit, `if (_split > 0 && nudge == address(0)) revert NudgeNotConfigured();`; symmetrically in setNudgeAddress reject clearing to address(0) while nudgeSplit > 0 (or auto-zero the split). This makes the L506 claim-time check defensive rather than load-bearing. Safe config order today: set the nudge ADDRESS first, then enable the split; to disable, zero the split before clearing the address.
verification: Static + manual reasoning (no machine PoC required for a Low availability footgun). Root cause read directly from source (L396 vs L506). Both LLM scanners independently derived the same path; story-faithfulness corroborates the L506 revert is the documented intended behavior, confirming this is a write-side enforcement gap, not a behavioral bug.

poc.note: Low / no value-extraction path; root cause verified by static reasoning. The brick is observable directly from setNudgeSplit (no nudge!=0 guard) vs the claim() L506 read-side revert.
